title: Islam: good character
hook: Muslims honor the Prophet's gentleness, and a hadith says the best of you are the best in character (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday: zakat, the yearly share for those in need. Your line was purified by giving.

The mosque in Medina, the Prophet's own. His companions sit around him. A desert traveler wanders in, a Bedouin who doesn't know the customs, walks to a corner, and starts to relieve himself on the floor. The companions leap up, shouting, ready to drag him out. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, stops them. Let him finish, he says. Then he has a bucket of water poured over the spot, calls the man over, and explains, kindly, what a mosque is for.
screen: `A STRANGER IN THE MOSQUE.` → `THE COMPANIONS LEAP UP.` → `LET HIM FINISH.`

segments.voice: That story is in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, and in one version the Prophet tells his companions: you were sent to make things easy, not to make them difficult. It's one of many. The hadith collections remember his gentleness: mending his own shoes, helping at home, playing with children, standing up when a funeral passed. The Qur'an says to him, in Marmaduke Pickthall's 1930 translation: "And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature." The Arabic word there is khuluq, character, from the same family as akhlaq, the Muslim word for ethics and good conduct. When his wife Aisha was later asked what his character was like, she answered, in a report in Sahih Muslim: his character was the Qur'an. He lived what he recited. And he set character very high. In a hadith in Bukhari, he says: the best of you are those who are best in character. Another says nothing will be heavier on the scale on the Day of Judgment than good character. And another, reported in several collections, has him describe his whole mission as coming to perfect good character. So in Islam, character isn't a pleasant extra added to prayer and fasting. It's what prayer and fasting are for. Tomorrow, that idea reaches even the fast. The Bedouin learned more from the bucket of water than from any shout.
screen: `MAKE THINGS EASY, NOT DIFFICULT.` · `THOU ART OF A TREMENDOUS NATURE.` · `HIS CHARACTER WAS THE QUR'AN.` · `NOTHING HEAVIER ON THE SCALE.` · then, large: `BEST IN CHARACTER.`

segments.voice: Recall a moment when someone did something wrong in front of you and you wanted to shout. Replay it, and this time picture the pause: let him finish. Then picture the bucket of water, the practical fix and the kind explanation, and let the gentler version settle in.
Islam, through good character: akhlaq, the gentleness Muslims honor in the Prophet. The best of you are the best in character. Today's word.
Your line: best in character. Easy, not difficult: that was the Medina way. Day two hundred seventy-two, done.

howItsDone: Muslims study akhlaq, Islamic ethics, alongside prayer and law, and many learn the Prophet's example of gentleness from the hadith collections and biographies taught in mosques and families.

chat.says: In Islam, is good character just a nice extra on top of prayer?
options: No. The best of you are the best in character; it's what worship is for.
Yes. Prayer and fasting count; how you treat people is a side matter.
No. Good character is owed only to fellow Muslims, not to strangers.
chat.meaning: A hadith says the best of you are the best in character. In Islam, character is what prayer and fasting are for.
